name: Task_5
description:
Evaluate the linear coupling between lattice strain and the optical phonon frequency of bulk Silicon using a machine learning regression model. Start with a primitive diamond unit cell of Silicon (a = 5.43 \u00c5). The MACE-MP-0 foundation model should be used as the ASE-compatible calculator to describe interatomic interactions. Generate a dataset of 25 distinct deformed crystal structures by systematically applying combinations of isotropic lattice-parameter scaling (scaling the baseline lattice parameter by the fractions: -0.02, -0.01, 0.0, 0.01, 0.02) and a subsequent uniaxial strain along the z-axis (applying Cartesian diag(1, 1, 1 + strain) to every cell vector and atomic position, with strain taking the fractions: -0.02, -0.01, 0.0, 0.01, 0.02). For each of the 25 configurations, compute the \u0393-point phonons using finite-displacement methods or analytical derivatives and extract the maximum positive vibrational frequency (which corresponds to the highest optical mode) in eV. Construct a feature matrix of shape (25, 2) where the first column is the isotropic lattice-strain fraction and the second column is the uniaxial strain fraction. Construct a target vector containing the 25 extracted frequencies. Train a linear regression model on this complete dataset to predict the frequency from the strain components. Report only the two regression coefficients in eV per unit strain; the evaluator derives the intercept. The evaluator reconstructs all 25 phonon energies and fit residuals from the calculation log. Submit the results and calculation log in the format specified below.

Use the same unrelaxed two-atom reference for every strain pair, natural silicon masses, primitive vectors a/2 × (0,1,1), a/2 × (1,0,1), a/2 × (1,1,0), and fractional positions (0,0,0) and (0.25,0.25,0.25); its Cartesian axes are the conventional cubic axes. Fit all 25 points by unweighted ordinary least squares with an intercept, and retain the calculations.

Both reported regression coefficients and the coefficients reconstructed from the retained calculations must lie within 10% of the independently calculated pinned-model coefficients for the current Cartesian-z strain definition.
